model.name: Test Case / Test Result
model.purpose: Repeatable test definition, execution and evidence
model.scope_statement: WM-SFT-015 as a whole covers the repeatable definition and design of a test case (identity, preconditions, steps, expected results, oracle, data and traceability), its execution and result records (attempts, observed outcomes, adjudicated verdicts, evidence), the assurance view over those results (suite/campaign aggregation, coverage claims, exit criteria), and the governance of the resulting record set. This split-pass result populates only the execution, result and evidence portion of that boundary; definition/design, assurance aggregation and canonical governance service layers are contributed by sibling passes of the same aggregate and are deliberately not structured here. Throughout, an observed fact and an adjudicated verdict are distinct: the model records what was observed, who asserted a verdict over those observations and in what mode, and never lets a later attempt overwrite earlier evidence.
in_scope: Test-case definition and design: identity, revision, preconditions, procedure steps, expected results, oracle and test-data references (sibling pass)

Test execution and result records: attempt identity, binding to an exact test-case revision, run/suite/build/environment/actor references, time points, parameter values, observed outcomes and per-step outcomes (this pass)
Evidence: logs, captures, traces, attachments, digests, attestation references, retries, non-determinism evidence and supersession/correction history (this pass)
Assurance view: suite and campaign aggregation, coverage and exit-criteria claims over result sets (sibling pass)
Governance of the record set: canonical service layers, code lists, roles and retention schedule (sibling pass)
Format-neutral semantics with declared projections onto JUnit-style XML, TAP, SARIF, Open Test Reporting and telemetry attribute conventions
out_of_scope: Defect / issue report lifecycle: triage, severity assignment, resolution and closure remain with the defect model; only typed references and their assertion time are carried here
Build and release lifecycle: WM-SFT-008 references this evidence for release assurance; release gating decisions, promotion states and approval workflow are not modelled here
Environment and configuration-item lifecycle: provisioning, drift detection and decommissioning belong to the environment/CMDB model; this model carries an environment reference only
Identity, authentication and authorization of actors and tools: only actor and tool references are carried; principal lifecycle and entitlement evaluation are external
Durable audit-trail semantics: this model records actor, time and reason on adjudications, but the append-only audit log and its retention are owned by the audit-log model
Runtime policy evaluation and enforcement: retry policies, quarantine policies, integrity-verification policies and release gates are referenced, never evaluated or enforced by this model
Requirements and traceability master data: requirement records and coverage authority live in the requirements model; this model carries the criterion reference used at execution time
CI/CD pipeline orchestration: scheduling, agent allocation and pipeline definition belong to the pipeline model; only the invocation actually observed is recorded

boundary_notes.distinction: The declared relation is that a build or release references test evidence for release assurance. This model therefore emits identified, digest-sealed result records and may carry a back-reference to the consuming build; it does not model release states, promotion, approvals or gate evaluation, and a release decision is never stored as a result attribute.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 keeps the incident report separate from the test execution log. This model records that an execution referenced a defect in a stated role at a stated time; defect state, severity and closure are read from the defect model. A pass verdict is never inferred from the absence of a linked defect.

SARIF records the machine and account of an invocation as run context, not as an owned entity. This model carries an environment reference plus the few observed runtime facts needed for reproducibility; environment composition, provisioning and drift are owned externally.
EARL separates the assertor from the assertion. This model records who or what asserted a verdict and in which mode; principal registration, credentials and entitlement decisions remain external.

Adjudication and supersession entries carry actor, timestamp and reason so the change is self-describing, but the tamper-evident audit trail, its ordering guarantees and its retention are owned by the audit-log model. Referencing an audit record does not grant this model audit-trail semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Test-case definition / design (sibling pass of WM-SFT-015)
boundary_notes.distinction: Expected results, procedure steps and oracle definitions are authored in the definition pass. The execution pass binds to an immutable revision of that definition and records what was observed against it; it never re-states or edits the expectation.

sources.title: Static Analysis Results Interchange Format (SARIF) Version 2.1.0 Plus Errata 01
sources.version_or_date: Version 2.1.0 Errata 01, OASIS Approved Errata, 28 August 2023
sources.relevance: Normative separation of run, invocation, result and artifact; result kind versus level; automation details and correlation identifiers for grouping logically equivalent results across runs.

sources.title: SARIF JSON Schema 2.1.0 (sarif-schema-2.1.0.json)
sources.organization: OASIS Static Analysis Results Interchange Format TC
sources.relevance: Exact property and enum definitions: invocation startTimeUtc/endTimeUtc/exitCode/executionSuccessful/commandLine/machine, result kind and level enums, baselineState, fingerprints and partialFingerprints, artifact hashes, attachment and runAutomationDetails.

sources.title: Evaluation and Report Language (EARL) 1.0 Schema
sources.relevance: Canonical separation of Assertion (assertedBy, subject, test, mode) from TestResult (outcome, pointer, info, date); outcome vocabulary passed/failed/cantTell/inapplicable/untested and test modes automatic/manual/semiAuto/undisclosed.

sources.title: Accessibility Conformance Testing (ACT) Rules Format 1.1
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of test target, applicability, expectations and the five outcome values; consistency validation of an implementation against test cases with expected outcomes; requirement to report outcomes with pointers identifying the test target.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar: full-date, full-time, mandatory stated offset to UTC, seconds field including leap-second range, upper-case Z, and the distinct meaning of an unknown local offset -00:00.

sources.title: IEEE/ISO/IEC 29119-3-2021 — Software and systems engineering — Software testing — Part 3: Test documentation
sources.relevance: International standard for test documentation arranged by test process, distinguishing test-design and test-case documentation from execution-time documentation such as execution logs and incident reports for manual, automated, scripted and unscripted testing.

sources.title: TAP Version 14 Specification
sources.relevance: Streamable result grammar: plan, test points with ok/not ok, test-point identifiers with uniqueness guidance, SKIP and TODO directives that harnesses must not treat as failures, YAML diagnostic blocks, subtests and bail out.

sources.title: in-toto Attestation Framework — Test Result predicate
sources.relevance: Binds a test result to the subject under test by digest, with a required result enum, required configuration resource descriptors and optional per-test name lists; states that test-name semantics are agreed between producer and consumer.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions — Test attributes registry
sources.relevance: Telemetry projection of test execution: test.case.name, test.case.result.status (pass, fail), test.suite.name and test.suite.run.status (success, failure, skipped, aborted, timed_out, in_progress); demonstrates a deliberately narrower status vocabulary than the record model.

sources.title: Open Test Reporting
sources.version_or_date: Version 0.2.7; core, events and hierarchy schemas 0.2.0
sources.relevance: Event-based, streamable, language-agnostic test reporting with started/finished events, infrastructure metadata, arbitrary container hierarchies and result outcomes SUCCESSFUL/FAILED/ABORTED; explicitly a modernisation of the Ant-derived XML report.

sources.title: Maven Surefire test report XSD (surefire-test-report.xsd)
sources.version_or_date: master branch, retrieved 2026-09-03; no targetNamespace declared
sources.relevance: First-party schema for the de facto JUnit-style XML projection: testsuite/testcase with failure, error, skipped, rerunFailure, rerunError, flakyFailure, flakyError, stackTrace, system-out/system-err and properties; shows the format carries no record identifier.

sources.title: Maven Surefire Plugin — Rerun failing tests
sources.relevance: Documents retry semantics in a widely deployed harness: flakyFailure/flakyError when a test eventually passes versus failure plus rerunFailure/rerunError when all attempts fail, and the reported time being that of the last successful or first failing run.

bundles.name: Execution Record and Run Context
bundles.description: The identified execution event itself: which frozen test-case revision was exercised, with which parameter values, inside which run, against which build, in which environment, by which actor or tool, at which times, and as which attempt in a retained attempt series.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 arranges test documentation by process, keeping execution-time documentation distinct from test-design documentation, and SARIF separates the run and its invocation from the results produced. Without an identified record bound to an immutable definition and a stated context, an observation cannot be interpreted, compared or reproduced.

layers.name: Execution identity and definitional binding
layers.description: How an execution record is identified in its own right, how it is pinned to an exact test-case revision and criterion version, and which external records give it context and reproducibility.

findings.name: Execution record identity and correlation
findings.description: Every execution/result record is an independently identified entity, distinct from the test case it exercises, from the run that contains it and from any report that renders it. Identity is never derived from a date, a verdict value or a test-case identifier; a separate correlation key groups logically equivalent executions across runs.

questions.text: Which system of record issues the authoritative identifier for this execution record, and what is that identifier?
answer_data: Reference to the issuing system of record

questions.text: When no master-system identifier exists, which governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID stands in, and how is that substitution marked?
Which stable correlation key groups executions that are logically the same check across different runs?
answer_data: Correlation identifier for the equivalence class
Scope over which the correlation key is stable

questions.text: What constraint prevents a date, a status value, a display name or a test-case identifier from acting as the record key?

data_elements.name: Execution record identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of this execution/attempt record as issued by its system of record, or the governed or locally minted substitute.

data_elements.name: Issuing system reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the test-management, harness or CI system that issued the execution identifier, so the identifier can be resolved and its authority judged.

data_elements.name: Result correlation key
data_elements.description: Stable key identifying the equivalence class of logically identical executions across runs, modelled on SARIF correlationGuid semantics.

data_elements.name: Result fingerprints
data_elements.description: Named fingerprint strings that let consumers recognise the same logical result after cosmetic changes, without relying on the record identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity here is reference data carried on the record itself: identifier values, the issuing-system reference, a correlation key and fingerprint strings. There is no separate document that constitutes the identity, and minting an identity certificate would create a second, competing source of truth alongside the master system.

findings.name: Binding to the exact test-case revision and parameter values
findings.description: The execution binds to an immutable revision of the test case, its expected-result or oracle definition and the criterion or rule being evaluated, together with the concrete parameter values, data-set references and seeds actually used. A later edit of the test case must not silently change the meaning of a past result.

questions.text: Which immutable test-case revision, and which version of its expected-result or oracle definition, does this execution bind to?
answer_data: Test-case identifier plus revision or digest
Reference to the definition record in the sibling design pass

questions.text: Which criterion or rule was evaluated, in which rule version and by which tool component version?
What concrete parameter values, data-set references and randomisation seeds were bound for this execution?
What happens to this record if the referenced test case is subsequently modified, deprecated or withdrawn?

data_elements.name: Bound test-case revision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the exact, immutable test-case revision exercised, resolvable independently of the current head revision of that case.

data_elements.name: Test-case definition digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest over the bound definition, so that a change to the definition is detectable from the result record alone.

data_elements.name: Evaluated criterion or rule reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the rule, requirement or accessibility criterion evaluated, following SARIF ruleId and ACT rule identification practice.

data_elements.name: Bound parameter values
data_elements.description: The concrete name/value bindings, data-set references and configuration inputs used for this execution, corresponding to in-toto configuration resource descriptors.

data_elements.name: Randomisation seed
data_elements.description: Seed or generator state that makes a randomised or property-based execution repeatable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a set of typed references, digests and value pairs held on the record. The test-case definition itself is a document owned by the definition/design pass of this aggregate; reproducing it here as a local artifact would duplicate an externally owned artifact and invite divergence between two copies of the same expectation.

findings.name: Execution context and reproducibility references
findings.description: The references that make an execution interpretable and repeatable: containing run and suite or campaign, the build or source revision under test identified by digest, the environment or configuration item, the executing actor, harness and tool version, and the observed invocation with its command line and exit status. All targets are externally owned records.

questions.text: Which run, suite or campaign contains this execution, and what identifies that container authoritatively?
answer_data: Container hierarchy path or parent reference

questions.text: Which build, artifact or source revision was under test, identified by digest rather than by label?
answer_data: Subject descriptor with name and digest

questions.text: Which environment or configuration item hosted the execution, and which model owns that record?
answer_data: Observed runtime facts such as machine and platform
Owning model or system for the environment record

questions.text: Which actor, harness or tool executed the case, in which version, and under what observed invocation?
answer_data: Executing actor or service account reference
Harness and tool name with version
Command line, working directory and exit code

questions.text: What minimum context set must be present before this record may be treated as reproducible?
answer_data: Reason code for each missing context element

data_elements.name: Containing run reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the run or invocation that contains this execution, aligned with SARIF run automation details and Open Test Reporting container events.

data_elements.name: Suite or campaign reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the suite, campaign or container grouping to which this execution belongs; nesting may be arbitrarily deep.

data_elements.name: Subject under test descriptor
data_elements.description: Name plus digest of the artifact, build or source revision under test, following in-toto subject and ResourceDescriptor semantics.

data_elements.name: Execution environment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the environment or configuration item that hosted the execution, plus the minimal observed runtime facts (machine, platform, account) needed to interpret the result.

data_elements.name: Executing actor or tool reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the human tester, service account, harness or analysis tool that performed the execution, with the tool version.

data_elements.name: Observed invocation record
data_elements.description: Command line, arguments, working directory, exit code and execution-successful flag as observed, modelled on the SARIF invocation object.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Context is expressed as typed references into models that own the referenced entities plus a small set of observed runtime facts. Materialising an environment or build description here would copy a target model's state into this record and would go stale the moment the target changes; the reference plus the observed invocation facts is the defensible minimum.

layers.name: Execution time and attempt series
layers.description: Time semantics for an execution attempt, and the append-only series of attempts produced by retries under one logical binding.

findings.name: Execution time points, duration and clock provenance
findings.description: Four time semantics are kept distinct: when the attempt started and ended (event time), when each outcome was observed by the executing agent, and when the record was ingested into the store. All are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and none may be collapsed into another.

questions.text: What are the start and end times of this attempt, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
answer_data: Offset or Z designator as recorded

questions.text: When was each outcome observed by the executing agent, and when was the record ingested, and do these differ from the event time?
answer_data: Recorded reason for any divergence or backfill

questions.text: What duration is reported, measured from which clock and at what resolution?
answer_data: Resolution or precision of the measurement

questions.text: How are unsynchronised, unknown-offset or reconstructed timestamps represented without fabricating precision?

data_elements.name: Attempt start time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time at which this attempt began, with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Attempt end time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time at which this attempt ended; absent while the attempt is still in progress or was lost.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which a specific outcome or measurement was observed by the executing agent, recorded per observation where it differs from the attempt boundaries.

data_elements.name: Record ingestion time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which the record entered the result store; always recorded separately from event and observation time.

data_elements.name: Attempt duration
data_elements.description: Measured elapsed time of the attempt with its unit and resolution; the JUnit-style projection carries only a bare float here, which is a known lossy mapping.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time points are scalar values on the record with a declared format rule. There is no document that could carry them more faithfully, and any external time certificate would itself need the same RFC 3339 representation, so an artifact adds indirection without adding evidentiary weight.

findings.name: Attempts, retries and append-only accumulation
findings.description: A retry produces a new attempt record; it never re-opens or overwrites an earlier one. The finding covers attempt ordinal, predecessor linkage, retry trigger and the referenced retry policy, and how a disagreeing attempt series is summarised without destroying any member.

questions.text: What is this attempt's ordinal within the retry group, and which earlier attempt does it directly follow?
answer_data: Retry group key shared by the series

questions.text: What triggered this retry — harness policy, orchestration rule or human decision — and which policy record applies?
answer_data: Reference to the governing retry policy record

questions.text: Which rule guarantees that an earlier attempt's observations, timestamps and attachments cannot be mutated by a later attempt?
When attempts in one group disagree, how is the group-level outcome reported and which attempt is authoritative?
answer_data: Disagreement flag and retained member outcomes

data_elements.name: Attempt ordinal
data_elements.description: One-based position of this attempt within its retry group; ordinals are never reused or renumbered.

data_elements.name: Predecessor attempt reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the attempt this one retries, making the series traversable in both directions.

data_elements.name: Retry trigger code
data_elements.description: Governed code stating what caused the retry, for example automatic harness rerun, orchestration policy or explicit human request.

data_elements.name: Retry policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally owned retry policy in force; this model records which policy applied, not the policy's evaluation or enforcement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Attempt sequencing is relational metadata linking records that already exist. The evidence produced by each attempt is represented by that attempt's own attachments; introducing a separate retry-log artifact would create a third copy of facts already held on the attempt records and on the referenced policy.

bundles.name: Observed Outcome and Adjudicated Verdict
bundles.description: What was actually observed and compared, step by step, and separately what verdict an assertor reached over those observations, including non-determinism evidence and the correction history of adjudications.
bundles.rationale: EARL models an Assertion as made by an assertor in a stated mode over a subject and criterion, with the TestResult carrying the outcome; ACT Rules Format keeps applicability and expectations separate from the reported outcome; SARIF separates the objective kind of a result from its interpreted level. Collapsing observation into verdict makes a result unfalsifiable and unreviewable.

layers.name: Observed outcome and comparison
layers.description: The observable facts of an execution: the actual value or system state, how it was compared with the expectation, under what tolerance, and where in the subject the observation applies, including per-step granularity.

findings.name: Actual outcome and comparison against expectation
findings.description: The observed actual output or system state, the expectation compared against, the comparator and its version, the tolerance, normalisation or masking applied before comparison, the resulting delta, and the pointer identifying where in the subject the observation applies.

questions.text: What actual value, output or system state was observed, and in what representation was it captured?
Against which expected value or oracle was the observation compared, and by which comparator?
What tolerance, precision, normalisation or masking was applied before the comparison was judged?
answer_data: Tolerance value with unit or percentage
Masked or ignored regions and fields

questions.text: Where in the subject does this observation apply, expressed as a pointer, location or region?
answer_data: Region, range or rectangle of interest
Artifact location URI for the pointed-at content

questions.text: How is an observation that could not be evaluated recorded without asserting either pass or fail?
answer_data: Diagnostic message and partial observation retained

data_elements.name: Observed actual outcome
data_elements.description: The actual value, output or system state observed, in a declared representation; large payloads are carried by reference to an evidence artifact.

data_elements.name: Expected value or oracle reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the expectation actually used at execution time, resolving into the bound test-case revision rather than into the current definition.

data_elements.name: Comparator identity and version
data_elements.description: The comparison function, matcher or assertion library and version that produced the comparison result.

data_elements.name: Applied tolerance
data_elements.description: Numeric or structural tolerance, precision limit or similarity threshold applied before the comparison was judged.

data_elements.name: Observation pointer
data_elements.description: Pointer, region or range identifying the part of the subject the observation concerns, modelled on EARL pointer and SARIF location semantics.

artifacts.name: Comparison record
artifacts.description: The materialised comparison between expectation and observation for one attempt: textual diff, structural diff or visual difference image, together with the tolerance actually applied.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative attachment identifier from the artifact store where one exists; otherwise the content digest combined with the owning execution identifier and attempt ordinal.

artifacts.name: Captured actual output
artifacts.description: The raw observed output or system-state capture that the comparison was performed against, retained so that the comparison can be independently re-derived.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Content digest plus owning attempt identifier; where the harness assigns a capture identifier, that master-system identifier takes precedence.

findings.name: Per-step and per-assertion outcomes
findings.description: Ordered step, assertion or sub-test outcomes inside one execution, each with its own status, message and position, plus the point of first deviation and the disposition of steps after it. A container outcome is derived from members and never replaces the members' own records.

questions.text: Which ordered steps or assertions were executed, and what outcome does each carry in its own right?
answer_data: Reference to the step in the bound procedure

questions.text: At which step did execution first deviate, and were the following steps executed, skipped or blocked?
How is the container or suite outcome derived from member outcomes, and is that derivation itself recorded?
What distinguishes a step from a nested sub-test, and how deep may the hierarchy legitimately go?

data_elements.name: Step ordinal
data_elements.description: Position of the step or assertion within the executed procedure; TAP test-point identifiers must fall within the declared plan range and should be unique.

data_elements.name: Per-step outcome
data_elements.description: Outcome code for one step, assertion or sub-test, held independently of the parent execution's adjudicated verdict.

data_elements.name: Per-step diagnostic message
data_elements.description: Human-readable message, directive reason or structured diagnostic attached to a step outcome, such as a TAP YAML diagnostic block.

data_elements.name: Container outcome derivation
data_elements.description: Record of how a container, suite or sub-test parent outcome was derived from its members, including member counts by outcome.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Step outcomes are a structured, ordered collection of small records on the execution rather than a document; the narrative and byte-level evidence for the same steps is represented once in the attachment finding. Duplicating the step list as a separate artifact would create two orderings that could drift apart under retry.

layers.name: Verdict, non-determinism and correction
layers.description: The asserted verdict over the observations, its authority and mode, the classification of non-deterministic behaviour across attempts, and the append-only correction history of adjudications.

findings.name: Adjudicated verdict, assertor and status vocabulary
findings.description: A verdict is an assertion made by a named assertor in a stated mode over recorded observations, expressed in a governed vocabulary covering passed, failed, error, blocked, skipped, inconclusive, not-applicable and untested, with explicit mappings to external vocabularies. The absence of a defect, of a failure element or of a report is never evidence of pass.

questions.text: Which governed verdict value applies to this execution, and what is that value's precise definition in the adopting Dimension?
answer_data: Normative definition text for the value

questions.text: Who or what asserted the verdict, in which mode, and on whose authority?
answer_data: Assertion mode such as automatic, manual or semi-automatic

questions.text: Which recorded observations and which oracle support this verdict, and was it derived or directly reported?
Which verdict and evidence combinations are prohibited, such as a pass with no evaluated expectation or a pass inferred from an absent defect?
answer_data: Validation error codes raised on violation

questions.text: How does this verdict map onto external vocabularies, and which mappings lose information?
answer_data: Mapping table with target vocabulary versions

data_elements.name: Verdict code
data_elements.description: Governed verdict value for the execution, distinct from any per-step outcome and from the observed facts that support it.

data_elements.name: Verdict assertor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent, tool or person that asserted the verdict, following EARL assertedBy semantics.

data_elements.name: Assertion mode
data_elements.description: How the verdict was reached: automatic, manual, semi-automatic, undisclosed or unknown.

data_elements.name: Verdict supporting basis
data_elements.description: References to the observations, comparisons and attachments relied on, so that the verdict can be re-derived and challenged.

data_elements.name: Interpreted severity
data_elements.description: Optional interpreted severity or level accompanying a failing verdict, kept separate from the objective verdict value as SARIF separates level from kind.

data_elements.name: Source-format verdict value
data_elements.description: The verbatim status token emitted by the originating harness or format, retained alongside the canonical code so lossy mappings stay auditable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A verdict is a single governed code plus assertion metadata and references to its basis; the evidence supporting it is represented once elsewhere. Issuing a separate verdict certificate would either duplicate the record or become a competing authority, and any signed statement over the verdict already belongs to the evidence-integrity finding.

findings.name: Non-determinism and flaky-test evidence
findings.description: Evidence that an identical binding produced differing outcomes across an attempt set, recorded as a property of that set rather than as a mutation of any attempt. Covers determinism classification, the measure and window used, and whether the classification is permitted to affect the reported verdict.

questions.text: Across which attempt set, under which proven-identical binding, did the observed outcomes disagree?
answer_data: Binding-equality evidence such as matching definition and parameter digests

questions.text: How is this execution classified — deterministic, flaky, environment-induced or unknown — and on what evidence?
May a non-determinism classification change the reported verdict, and which role is permitted to decide that?
What instability measure is reported, over which observation window and with which denominator?

data_elements.name: Determinism classification
data_elements.description: Governed code recording whether the execution is treated as deterministic, flaky, environment-induced or unclassified.

data_elements.name: Instability measure
data_elements.description: Quantified instability such as a flake rate, with its window and denominator, so the figure is interpretable and comparable.

data_elements.name: Quarantine or suppression reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an externally owned quarantine, suppression or known-issue record; this model records that the reference exists, not the suppression policy or its enforcement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Non-determinism is a derived property of an attempt set whose underlying evidence already exists on the individual attempts. Materialising a flakiness dossier would freeze a derived judgement as a document and risk it being consumed as primary evidence, which is exactly the observation/adjudication confusion this bundle exists to prevent.

findings.name: Correction, supersession and result revisions
findings.description: Execution records are append-only: an adjudication is corrected by adding a superseding revision that cites the record it supersedes, the reason, the correcting actor and the effective time. A rerun is a new attempt, never a correction, and superseded revisions remain retrievable.

questions.text: Which states may an execution record occupy, and which transitions between them are legal?
answer_data: State code list such as in-progress, recorded, adjudicated, superseded, withdrawn
Preconditions and required evidence per transition

questions.text: Which revision supersedes which, for what reason, by whom, and effective from when?
answer_data: Correcting actor reference and effective timestamp

questions.text: What distinguishes a correction of an adjudication from a new execution attempt, and which must be used in each case?
For how long must a superseded revision remain retrievable, and which policy owns that decision?
answer_data: Disposition action recorded when the period expires

data_elements.name: Execution record state
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the record, distinct from the verdict it carries.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the revision this record replaces; the replaced revision is retained and remains resolvable.

data_elements.name: Correction reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason plus justification for a superseding adjudication, such as misclassified error, wrong binding or oracle defect.

data_elements.name: Correcting actor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the actor who issued the correction, recorded with the RFC 3339 effective timestamp of the change.

data_elements.name: Baseline comparison state
data_elements.description: Optional state of this result relative to a declared baseline run, aligned with SARIF baselineState values new, unchanged, updated and absent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Supersession is expressed as versioned links and reason codes between records that already exist in the store. A standalone correction notice would be a second place where the same change is asserted, and the durable, tamper-evident record of who changed what is owned by the referenced audit-log model rather than by this one.

bundles.name: Evidence, Integrity and Interchange
bundles.description: The byte-level evidence produced by an execution, the digests and attestations that seal it, the outbound references to defects and consumers, and the format projections through which results leave this model.
bundles.rationale: SARIF binds artifacts and attachments to results with cryptographic hashes; the in-toto test-result predicate binds a result to the subject under test by digest and requires the configuration used. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 keeps incident reporting separate from execution logging. Interchange formats such as TAP, Open Test Reporting and JUnit-style XML are distinct projections with differing and lossy semantics.

layers.name: Evidence capture and integrity
layers.description: Which byte-level evidence was captured for an attempt, how it is bound and classified, and how digests and signed attestations make the evidence set tamper-evident.

findings.name: Logs, captures, traces and attachments
findings.description: Byte-level evidence attached to an attempt or observation: harness standard output and error, screenshots, recordings, distributed traces, coverage data and crash dumps. Each attachment declares its role, media type, size, durable location, capture time, sensitivity classification and the attempt, step or observation it is bound to.

questions.text: Which evidence artifacts were captured for this attempt, and what role does each one play?
To which attempt, step or observation is each attachment bound, and may one attachment serve several of them?
answer_data: Region, offset or timecode within the attachment

Where is each artifact stored, and which reference stays meaningful if the store is rotated or purged?

data_elements.name: Attachment reference
data_elements.description: Durable reference to a stored evidence artifact, resolvable independently of the harness working directory.

data_elements.name: Attachment role
data_elements.description: Governed code describing what the attachment evidences, for example harness output, screenshot at failure, trace or coverage data.

data_elements.name: Attachment media type and length
data_elements.description: Media type and byte length of the stored artifact, enabling safe handling without opening it.

data_elements.name: Attachment sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Classification of the artifact's contents for access and retention purposes; the governing policy itself is owned by the adopting Dimension.

artifacts.name: Execution log capture
artifacts.description: Standard output, standard error and structured harness log emitted during one attempt, retained per attempt so that a retry never displaces the earlier log.
media_or_form: harness standard output and error capture
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system attachment identifier from the artifact store; otherwise content digest combined with the owning execution identifier and attempt ordinal.

artifacts.name: Visual capture
artifacts.description: Screenshot, rendered page capture or screen recording taken during an attempt, typically at the point of first deviation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system attachment identifier where the capture service assigns one; otherwise content digest plus attempt ordinal and capture timestamp.

artifacts.name: Telemetry trace reference set
artifacts.description: Distributed trace, span set or metric series captured during the attempt and correlated to it by test attributes, referenced rather than copied where the telemetry store owns retention.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Trace or span identifier issued by the telemetry backend as the master-system identifier; otherwise the correlation attribute set plus the attempt identifier.

findings.name: Digests, sealing and result attestation
findings.description: Evidence integrity rests on named cryptographic digests over each artifact and result document, and on a signed statement binding the result to the subject under test by digest with the configuration used. Signing keys, trust roots and verification policy remain with the referenced supply-chain and identity models; this model records digests, attestation references and any verification outcome reported back to it.

questions.text: Which digest algorithm and value seals each evidence artifact and each emitted result document?
answer_data: Byte range or canonical form that was digested

questions.text: Which signed attestation, if any, binds this result to the subject under test, and under which predicate type?
answer_data: Subject descriptor with name and digest

questions.text: What integrity-check outcome has a verifying system reported back, and how is it recorded here without this model performing the check?
answer_data: Timestamp at which the outcome was recorded

questions.text: What minimum integrity metadata must be present before this result may be exported as release evidence?
answer_data: Completeness rule for the evidence manifest
Handling of artifacts lacking a digest

data_elements.name: Artifact digest
data_elements.description: Named-algorithm digest over an evidence artifact or emitted result document, following SARIF artifact hashes and in-toto ResourceDescriptor digest practice.

data_elements.name: Result attestation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a signed statement binding this result to the subject under test, with its predicate type URI; the signing and verification lifecycle is external.

data_elements.name: Reported verification outcome
data_elements.description: Outcome of an integrity check as reported by an external verifier, recorded with the verifier reference and the recording time; this model performs no verification itself.

artifacts.name: Evidence manifest
artifacts.description: Enumeration of every evidence artifact belonging to an execution record with its role, location, length and digest, so that omission or substitution of evidence is detectable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Owning execution identifier as the master key, with the manifest's own content digest distinguishing successive reissues.

artifacts.name: Signed test-result attestation
artifacts.description: Signed statement carrying a test-result predicate that binds the adjudicated result and its configuration to the digest-identified subject under test, for consumption by release assurance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Predicate type URI plus subject digest and owning execution identifier; the signing infrastructure's own identifier is recorded as a reference, not adopted as this record's key.

layers.name: Outbound references and result interchange
layers.description: How execution records point outward to defects, waivers and consuming builds, and how the format-neutral record is projected into interchange formats without those projections becoming authoritative.

findings.name: Defect, waiver and consumer references
findings.description: Typed outbound references from an execution record: defect or issue reports raised, reproduced or verified against it, waiver and known-issue references, and the builds or releases that consume the evidence. Only the reference, its role and its assertion time live here; every target keeps its own lifecycle.

questions.text: Which defect or issue records does this execution reference, and in which role — raised, reproduced, verified-fixed or known-issue?
answer_data: Timestamp at which the link was asserted and by whom

questions.text: Which model or system owns each referenced record's lifecycle, and which of its fields must never be copied into this record?
answer_data: Prohibited-copy field list such as defect state and severity
Resolution rule when the local reference and the target disagree

questions.text: What rule prevents a pass verdict from being inferred from the absence of a linked defect or an empty failure list?
answer_data: Required positive evidence for a pass
Validation error code raised on violation

questions.text: Which build or release records consume this evidence, and is that reference maintained here, at the consumer, or in both places?

data_elements.name: Defect or issue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an externally owned defect record together with the role it plays for this execution and the time the link was asserted.

data_elements.name: Outbound link role
data_elements.description: Governed code stating the role of an outbound reference, for example raised, reproduced, verified-fixed, waived or known-issue.

data_elements.name: Consuming build or release reference
data_elements.description: Optional back-reference to a build or release that cites this evidence; the release lifecycle and any gating decision remain outside this model.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed pointers into models that own the referenced entities. Producing a local linkage document would materialise another model's state inside this one, would go stale as targets change, and would blur the ownership boundary this finding exists to enforce.

findings.name: Result documents and format projections
findings.description: The canonical execution record is format-neutral; JUnit-style XML, TAP 14, SARIF, Open Test Reporting documents and telemetry attribute sets are projections of it. This finding records which projection was emitted, its schema version, the semantics lost in the mapping, how identifiers survive projection and which side is authoritative on disagreement.

answer_data: Reference to the mapping table used
List of fields and distinctions dropped in projection

answer_data: Identifier carriage mechanism such as a property or extension element
Collision handling for identical names across products

questions.text: Which representation is authoritative when the emitted projection and the internal record disagree?
How is an emitted document checked against its declared schema, and what is recorded when it does not validate?

data_elements.name: Emitted projection format
data_elements.description: Name and schema or specification version of each interchange format emitted from this record.

data_elements.name: Projection mapping reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed mapping table applied for the projection, with its lossy-mapping flags.

data_elements.name: Projection authority declaration
data_elements.description: Statement of which representation governs on disagreement; in this model the internal record is authoritative and the projection is derived.

artifacts.name: Canonical execution result report
artifacts.description: The format-neutral, self-contained rendering of an execution record set with its bindings, attempts, outcomes, verdicts and evidence manifest, used as the source from which projections are derived.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Owning run or execution identifier from the system of record, combined with the report's content digest to distinguish reissues.

artifacts.name: Interchange format projection
artifacts.description: A derived, non-authoritative document expressing the result set in an external format for a consuming toolchain, carrying its declared schema version and mapping reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived identity: source execution or run identifier plus format name, schema version and content digest; the projection never mints an independent record identity.

composition.purpose: Registered parent of WM-SFT-015. A test execution is an instance of a performed activity; this model specialises that activity for test execution and result recording and inherits the parent's generic activity identity and time framing rather than restating it.

Carries the digest-identified subject under test and an optional back-reference to the consuming build or release. Per the declared relation the build references this evidence for release assurance; release states, promotion, approvals and gate evaluation stay entirely with WM-SFT-008.

composition.target: Test environment / configuration-item model (registry identifier not yet assigned)
composition.purpose: Supplies the environment or configuration item in which an execution ran, so results are interpretable and comparable. Provisioning, drift and decommissioning lifecycles remain in the target; only the reference plus observed runtime facts are carried here.

composition.target: Defect / issue report model (registry identifier not yet assigned)
composition.purpose: Provides defect and issue records that an execution raised, reproduced or verified. This model records the reference, its role and its assertion time; triage, severity, state and closure belong to the target and are never mirrored here.

composition.target: Actor, identity and access model (registry identifier not yet assigned)
composition.purpose: Resolves the executing agent and the verdict assertor. Principal registration, credential lifecycle and entitlement evaluation stay in the target; this model stores only the reference and the assertion mode.

composition.target: Audit log / event log model (registry identifier not yet assigned)
composition.purpose: Receives actor, timestamp and reason for adjudications, supersessions and dispositions so they are durably recorded. Referencing an audit record grants this model no audit-trail semantics: ordering guarantees, tamper evidence and audit retention are the target's.

Alignment for run, invocation, result kind and level, artifact hashes, attachments, baseline state and correlation identifiers. Alignment only: conformance is not claimed, and SARIF's severity levels are mapped rather than adopted as this model's verdict vocabulary.

composition.target: W3C EARL 1.0 Schema and ACT Rules Format 1.1
composition.purpose: Alignment for the assertion structure (assertor, subject, criterion, mode) and the outcome vocabulary including cantTell, inapplicable and untested, which supply the observation/adjudication separation and the inconclusive semantics used here.

composition.target: in-toto Attestation Framework test-result predicate v0.1
composition.purpose: Alignment for binding a result to a digest-identified subject with the configuration used, and for expressing evidence integrity. Signing, key custody, trust policy and verification remain outside this model's boundary.

composition.target: TAP 14, Open Test Reporting and JUnit-style XML (Maven Surefire schema)
composition.purpose: Alignment for ecosystem projections of execution results, including streamed test points with SKIP/TODO directives, started/finished events with SUCCESSFUL/FAILED/ABORTED outcomes, and rerun/flaky elements. These are projections with lossy mappings, not the semantics of this model.

composition.target: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for test attributes
composition.purpose: Alignment for the telemetry projection of test execution and for correlating traces to attempts. Its status vocabulary is deliberately narrower than this model's verdict list, so the mapping is recorded as lossy in both directions.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner for the execution/result record set and one for the evidence artifact store; the two may differ but both must be named before records are accepted.
The Dimension publishes, before first use, its verdict code list, determinism classification list, attachment role list, retry policy reference and evidence retention schedule.
The Dimension declares which external system is master for execution identifiers and how locally minted UUID/ULID identifiers are marked as locally assigned.
The Dimension states which neighbouring models own defect, environment, release, identity and audit-log lifecycles so that no such field is written locally.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Execution identifiers are namespaced by the issuing master system, never by project, branch or date. Test-case names are not identifiers: projections that carry only a name and class must also carry the namespaced identifier so that identically named cases in different products cannot collide on merge.
registry_links: Governed code lists for verdict values, determinism classifications, attachment roles, link roles, retry triggers and correction reasons, each versioned with deprecation dates.
Alignment mapping registry for SARIF, EARL/ACT, TAP 14, Open Test Reporting, JUnit-style XML and OpenTelemetry test attributes, each entry versioned and carrying explicit lossy-mapping flags.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form orders attempts by ordinal, steps by ordinal and attachments by durable reference; verdict values are normalised to the governed code list while the verbatim source-format token is retained alongside.

Timestamps are normalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; the originally recorded offset is preserved rather than rewritten to UTC, and -00:00 is retained where the local offset was unknown.
Digests are canonicalised as algorithm-name plus lowercase hexadecimal value, computed over the declared canonical byte form of the artifact.
patch_rules: A patch may only add attempts, observations, attachments, outbound links or a superseding adjudication revision; any patch that mutates a recorded observation, timestamp, digest or attempt ordinal is rejected.
Every patch cites the record revision it applies to, the acting principal and a reason code, and carries its own RFC 3339 timestamp.
A patch that would change a sealed attempt is converted into a new attempt or a superseding revision; it is never applied in place.
compatibility_rules: Adding a verdict code, attachment role, determinism class or projection format is a minor change; narrowing, removing or redefining an existing code is breaking and requires a new code-list version with an explicit mapping from the old values.
Consumers must tolerate unknown attachment roles, unknown projection formats and additional per-step fields without discarding the execution record.
A projection schema upgrade never changes the internal record; the mapping table version is recorded on each emitted document so historic exports remain interpretable.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the test-management, harness or CI system of record for the execution, attempt or attachment, stored together with a reference to that issuing system.
Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system key exists, such as a resolvable execution URI or a run automation identifier and GUID.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, explicitly marked as locally assigned and never presented as a master-system key.
Never acceptable as identity: a date or timestamp, a verdict or status value, a test-case identifier alone, a display name, a file path, or an ordinal on its own.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-time strings carrying whole seconds (fractional seconds optional) and an explicit numeric UTC offset or the literal Z; -00:00 is used only where UTC is known but the local offset is not. Event time (attempt start and end), observation time (when the executing agent observed the outcome) and ingestion time (when the record entered the store) are stored in separate fields and must never be collapsed into one another; where they differ, all three are recorded, and a reconstructed or backfilled value is flagged as such rather than presented at full precision.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named from the owning execution identifier, the attempt ordinal and a zero-padded sequence within that attempt, plus the artifact role. Sequences never restart, never renumber on retry and are never reused after withdrawal; a reissued non-serial artifact such as an evidence manifest is distinguished by its content digest rather than by overwriting the previous instance.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artifact carries at least one named-algorithm digest recorded in the evidence manifest. Artifacts are immutable once sealed: any change produces a new artifact instance with a new digest and a link to the one it replaces, and no existing instance is rewritten. Where an artifact is later purged, its digest, role and length are retained in the manifest so the omission is detectable.

policies: Observation and adjudication are separate acts: no function may write an observed outcome and a verdict as one indivisible step without recording both the observing agent and the asserting agent, together with the assertion mode.

A pass verdict must rest on a recorded, evaluated expectation. It may never be inferred from the absence of a linked defect, from an empty failure list, from a missing report or from a successful process exit code alone.

A rerun never overwrites earlier evidence: every attempt is retained with its own identifier, ordinal, time points and attachments, and a correction to an adjudication is a superseding revision rather than an edit.
Format projections are derived and non-authoritative; where a projection and the internal record disagree, the internal record governs and the discrepancy is recorded against the mapping entry.

This model records references to retry policies, quarantine decisions, integrity verifiers, release gates and audit logs, and records outcomes reported back to it; it never evaluates, executes or enforces any of them.

read: Execution records, attempts and verdicts are read as immutable snapshots; every read returns the record identifier, its revision, its lifecycle state and, where applicable, the revision that superseded it.

Evidence artifacts are resolved through their durable reference and digest rather than a harness-relative path, and a read of a purged artifact returns its retained manifest entry with an explicit purged status.
create: An execution record is created only with an execution identifier, a resolvable immutable test-case revision reference, an attempt ordinal, a subject-under-test descriptor with digest and an RFC 3339 start time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
A retry creates a new attempt record linked to its predecessor; an existing attempt is never reopened, and a projection document never creates an independent record identity.
update: Observations, time points, digests and attachments are append-only and are sealed when the attempt finishes; after sealing they are not editable by any role.

Only adjudication-layer content may change — verdict, determinism classification and outbound links — and only by creating a superseding revision that cites the superseded revision, a reason code, the correcting actor and an effective RFC 3339 timestamp.
delete: This model performs no in-place deletion of execution records. Withdrawal is a lifecycle state transition that leaves a tombstone retaining the execution identifier, the bound test-case revision reference, the attempt ordinal, the last verdict state, the withdrawal reason and the digests of any removed evidence, so that the removal is detectable and the record remains countable.

Retention periods, legal hold and the physical disposition of evidence artifacts are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and executed by the referenced evidence artifact store or telemetry backend; WM-SFT-008 consumes this evidence but does not own its disposition. This model records only the disposition outcome reported back to it, with the executing policy reference and an RFC 3339 timestamp.

Superseded adjudication revisions remain retrievable for at least the retention period declared by the adopting Dimension; purging one requires a recorded disposition entry naming the executing policy and the acting principal, and never removes the tombstone or the manifest digest entry.

roles.name: Test execution owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the execution record set for a product or service, including completeness of bindings and context references
Declares which harnesses and systems may create execution records and which is master for execution identifiers

roles.name: Result adjudicator
responsibilities: Asserts verdicts over recorded observations and records the assertion mode and supporting basis
Issues superseding revisions with reason and effective time, and decides whether a determinism classification affects a reported verdict

roles.name: Evidence custodian
responsibilities: Owns attachment storage, sensitivity classification, redaction and durable references, and maintains the evidence manifest with digests
Records disposition outcomes reported by the artifact store and ensures purged artifacts retain a detectable manifest entry

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Maintains the alignment mapping registry and lossy-mapping flags for each projection format and schema version
Validates emitted projections against their declared schemas and records non-conformances without altering the internal record

roles.name: Model steward
responsibilities: Maintains the governed code lists, versioning and deprecation for verdicts, roles, triggers and classifications
Reviews boundary compliance so that defect, release, environment, identity and audit-log semantics are not written locally

access.default_rule: Execution records, bindings, time points and adjudicated verdicts are readable by any principal permitted to read the subject under test. Raw evidence artifacts default to a stricter grant than the record that references them, because captures may contain production, personal or secret content.
exceptions: Attachments classified as containing personal data or secrets are restricted to the evidence custodian and named investigators; general consumers receive redacted derivatives whose digests are recorded alongside the originals'.
Security-test results under an embargo may be withheld from general consumers until the referenced disclosure decision, owned elsewhere, is recorded as made.
Exported projections may omit restricted attachments while retaining their manifest entries and digests, so that omission is always detectable rather than silent.
audit_requirements: Every verdict adjudication, supersession, determinism classification and recorded disposition captures the acting principal, an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and a reason code; the durable, tamper-evident audit trail is written and retained by the referenced audit-log model, not by this model.

Access to restricted evidence artifacts is logged by the artifact store under its own policy; this model records only the artifact reference, its sensitivity classification and its availability status.

read_order: AGENTS.md — resolve Name, Type and the Specification URL for WM-SFT-015 before any other file
Specification URL — read the model boundary, in-scope and out-of-scope statements and the boundary notes before writing or interpreting any record
Storage type URL — learn the concrete projection in use (document store, relational, Git-tracked files or MCP-exposed collection) and confirm it is a projection, not the semantics
Interface URL — learn the read, create, append and supersede operations and the append-only constraints they enforce
Processes URL — learn the execute, record, compare, adjudicate, retry, seal and export processes and which neighbouring models own the lifecycles they reference
Governed code list and alignment mapping registry URLs — resolve verdict values and projection mappings before emitting or consuming any interchange document

coverage.claim: This result covers only the execution, result and evidence portion of WM-SFT-015: attempt identity and binding, run and context references, time semantics, observed outcomes and comparisons, per-step outcomes, adjudicated verdicts, non-determinism evidence, supersession, evidence artifacts and integrity, outbound references and interchange projections. Test-case definition and design, assurance aggregation and the canonical governance service layers are deliberately left to sibling passes of the same aggregate. Structure is grounded in OASIS SARIF, W3C EARL and ACT Rules Format, IETF RFC 3339, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3, TAP 14, in-toto, Open Test Reporting, Apache Maven Surefire and OpenTelemetry test attributes. No conformance to any of these is claimed; they are recorded as alignments.

checklist.notes: Execution-record identity, issuing-system reference, correlation key and fingerprints are modelled, with an explicit prohibition on date, status, name or test-case identifier as key. Grounded in SARIF result guid/correlationGuid/partialFingerprints and runAutomationDetails. Weakness: the dominant JUnit-style XML projection carries no record identifier at all, so identity survives projection only via an extension property.

Record states (in-progress, recorded, adjudicated, superseded, withdrawn), legal transitions, correction-versus-retry rules and append-only accumulation are modelled. Release, defect and environment lifecycles are explicitly excluded and pushed to composition links.

Run/suite containment, subject under test by digest, environment, actor and tool, predecessor attempt, defect and consumer links are all typed references with declared owning models and a prohibited-copy field list.

Attempt start/end (event time), observation time and ingestion time are separate required or optional fields under RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z, including the -00:00 unknown-offset convention and a backfill flag.

Assertor, assertion mode, observing agent, comparator version, tool version, invocation facts, correcting actor and supersession linkage are all captured. EARL supplies the normative assertor/mode separation.

Execution-record owner and evidence-store owner are distinct named roles; every outbound reference declares the model that owns the target's lifecycle and which of its fields must not be mirrored locally.

Prohibited verdict/evidence combinations, required positive evidence for a pass, schema validation of emitted projections and recorded non-conformances are modelled. Integrity verification itself is explicitly not owned: only reported outcomes are recorded.

Default grant separates record readability from artifact readability; exceptions cover personal data, secrets and embargoed security results, with digests retained so redaction and omission remain detectable.

No in-place deletion; withdrawal leaves a tombstone with identifier, binding, ordinal, verdict state and removed-evidence digests. Execution of disposition is explicitly owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the artifact store, not by this model and not by WM-SFT-008.

Projections onto SARIF, TAP 14, Open Test Reporting, JUnit-style XML and OpenTelemetry test attributes are modelled with versioned mapping tables, lossy-field lists and an explicit authority declaration favouring the internal record.
Actual value, expected value, comparator identity and version, tolerance, normalisation and masking, delta and duration with resolution are modelled as observations distinct from the verdict.

Named digests per artifact and per emitted document, an evidence manifest and an optional signed test-result attestation bound to the subject by digest, following in-toto. Key custody, trust roots and verification policy are outside the boundary.

Attempt-set disagreement, flake classification, instability measure and the reproducibility context (seed, digests, environment reference) are structured, but no primary standard normatively defines flaky-test classification or a flake-rate denominator. Maven Surefire's flakyFailure/rerunFailure distinction is a harness convention, not a specification, so this node is marked a gap rather than presented as canonical.

Physical or geographic location of execution is not a property of a result record. Where it matters (device farms, laboratory rigs, regulated sites), it is carried by the referenced environment or configuration-item model as an attribute of that entity.

Sensitivity classification, redaction method and residual-risk notes are modelled on attachments, because screenshots, logs and traces routinely capture production or personal data. The governing data-protection policy itself is owned by the adopting Dimension.

known_omissions: Test-case definition and design: preconditions, procedure steps, expected-result authoring, oracle design, test-data design and requirement traceability are left to the sibling definition pass and are only bound to here.

Assurance aggregation: suite and campaign roll-ups, coverage claims, exit criteria and test completion reporting are left to the sibling assurance pass; only per-container derivation of an outcome from members is modelled here.
Canonical governance service layers: the merger takes these from the governance pass, so the service_layers block supplied here is deliberately concise and execution-scoped.

Performance, load and reliability result semantics: percentile aggregation, warm-up exclusion and statistical significance of a regression are not modelled; they would need a dedicated measurement model.
Hardware-in-the-loop and real-time testing: sub-millisecond timing, clock domains, sampling jitter and physical instrumentation traceability are out of reach of RFC 3339 alone and are not addressed.
Manual exploratory session semantics: session charters, time-boxing and note-taking conventions are referenced only through the manual assertion mode.

Clause-level field lists from ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3:2021 could not be read directly (the ISO page returned HTTP 403 and the IEEE abstract does not enumerate template fields), so that standard supports process separation rather than specific field names here.
conflicts: JUnit-style XML has no single normative schema. The Apache Maven Surefire schema declares no target namespace and, by the project's own issue record, has lagged the elements the plugin actually emits (rerunError, flakyError, flakyFailure). Ant, Surefire and consumer implementations disagree on skipped and rerun handling, so this format is treated strictly as a projection.

Status vocabularies conflict across sources and cannot be losslessly unified: SARIF separates kind (pass, fail, notApplicable, review, open, informational) from level (none, note, warning, error); EARL uses passed, failed, cantTell, inapplicable, untested; ACT Rules Format 1.1 uses the same five with untested meaning not evaluated; JUnit-style XML distinguishes failure from error and has only skipped; Open Test Reporting uses SUCCESSFUL, FAILED, ABORTED; OpenTelemetry test.case.result.status admits only pass and fail while test.suite.run.status adds skipped, aborted, timed_out and in_progress. Every mapping is flagged lossy.

TAP 14 states that harnesses must not treat a failing TODO or SKIP test point as a failure, so a raw not-ok token does not map to a failed verdict. Any importer that maps not-ok directly to failure contradicts the specification.

Retry semantics conflict with result immutability in common practice: Maven Surefire reports a flaky test's time as that of the last successful run and an all-failing test's time as that of the first failing run, collapsing an attempt series into one testcase element. This model rejects that collapse and retains each attempt, so round-tripping through that projection is asymmetric.

SARIF baselineState (new, unchanged, updated, absent) expresses change relative to a baseline run, which overlaps but does not coincide with this model's supersession semantics; an absent result is not a withdrawn record.

in-toto's test-result predicate admits only PASSED, WARNED and FAILED and carries test names as free strings whose semantics are agreed bilaterally, so it cannot express blocked, inconclusive or untested and cannot by itself preserve record identity.
regional_assumptions: Retention and access rules assume a data-protection regime of the EU GDPR type, where captured screenshots and logs may constitute personal data. Jurisdictions with different regimes will alter the retention schedule and redaction obligations without changing the model structure.

No sector-specific evidence regime is assumed. Regulated domains such as medical device software (IEC 62304), airborne software (DO-178C), automotive functional safety (ISO 26262) and clinical or laboratory settings impose additional mandatory evidence, independence-of-reviewer and record-retention requirements that the adopting Dimension must add as constraints.

Timestamps assume a network-synchronised clock. Air-gapped, embedded or offline execution environments may produce unsynchronised or unknown-offset times, which the model represents with -00:00 and a confidence note rather than by silently normalising.
English-language governed code lists are assumed; localisation of verdict and role labels is a presentation concern and must not create parallel code values.
adversarial_checks: Can a verdict be recorded without an assertor or mode? No: verdict code and assertor reference are both required, and the adjudication function names the mode even for automated assertions. This is the EARL separation and is what prevents an unattributable pass.

Can a rerun erase a failure? No: retry creates a new attempt with the next ordinal and a predecessor link, observations are sealed when an attempt finishes, and patch rules reject in-place mutation. The Surefire convention of collapsing an attempt series into one element is explicitly recorded as a lossy projection rather than adopted.

Can a pass be inferred from an absent defect, an empty failure list or a zero exit code? No: an explicit policy and a validation rule require a recorded, evaluated expectation for a pass, and the outbound-links finding carries the inference prohibition and its error code. A zero exit code is stored as an observed invocation fact, never as a verdict.

Does any node claim ownership of a target model's semantics? Checked node by node against the WM-SFT-008 relation rationale and each composition link: retry policies, quarantine decisions, integrity verification, release gating, defect state, environment provisioning, principal entitlement and audit-trail durability are all expressed as references or as outcomes reported back, and appear in out_of_scope or boundary_notes. The integrity finding deliberately asks only what a verifier reported, not what this model verified; the audit requirement states the audit-log model writes and retains the trail.

Can a record be identified by a date, a status or a test-case identifier? No: identity_priority item four names each of these as never acceptable, no local ID contains a date-like component, and the model requires a subject-under-test digest plus an execution identifier rather than a name-and-time pair.

Is deletion silently possible? No: crud.delete forbids in-place deletion, mandates a tombstone retaining identifier, binding, ordinal, verdict state and removed-evidence digests, and names the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the artifact store as the owners of disposition execution, explicitly excluding WM-SFT-008 from that ownership.

Does the structure survive a format with no identifiers? Tested against JUnit-style XML and TAP 14, both of which identify tests by name or ordinal only. The interchange finding requires an identifier carriage mechanism and collision handling, and declares the internal record authoritative, so a lossy projection cannot silently redefine identity.
